data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Resumability is determined by whether the persisted state (event log, budget, and any non-deterministic state captures) forms a complete checkpoint at an event boundary. A halted run is resumable iff the checkpoint is complete: the event log is intact and self-verifying up to its last entry, the budget state equals the sum of all event costs subtracted from the initial budget, and every source of non-determinism that influenced the committed events is either (a) fully recorded in the events themselves or (b) reconstructable from a persisted seed. Resumption must be refused when the checkpoint is incomplete\u2014any of these components is missing, inconsistent, or refers to external state that can no longer be reproduced.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The event log is self-verifying but the budget state was not persisted or is stale relative to the last event.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Non-deterministic inputs (external API calls, environment variables, wall-clock timestamps) influenced committed events but their outputs were not captured, so the continuation cannot reproduce the run's trajectory.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The RNG seed or state was not persisted, and the system's event generation depends on sampling, so resumed events would follow a different probabilistic path.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The checkpoint is at a non-event-boundary: intermediate generation state was persisted but no event was committed, so there is no valid link target for the next appended event.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"A 'checkpoint' is the minimal persistent state from which the run can be exactly continued. For an append-only event log, the checkpoint includes the log itself (which encodes all committed decisions), the budget residue, and any non-determinism capture (RNG state, tool-call response caches). If all three are present and mutually consistent at an event boundary, the resumed run produces the same event sequence as a continuous run, preserving identity. If any component is absent or inconsistent, the resumed run would diverge\u2014either producing different event content (non-determinism not reconstructable) or violating resource constraints (budget mismatch)\u2014so resumption must be refused to avoid appending events that break the chain's coherence as a single run's record.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
